{{short description|Japanese life scientist}}
{{Nihongo|'''Masayuki Yamato'''|大和 雅之|Yamato Masayuki}} is a Japanese life scientist and a [[professor]] at [[Tokyo Women's Medical University]].{{cn|date=February 2020}} He specializes in regenerative medicine, tissue engineering, and cell biology, and known for research on cell sheets engineering. 

He instructed [[Haruko Obokata]] there and wrote a paper on [[STAP cell]] with her, [[Charles Vacanti]] and [[Yoshiki Sasai]].<ref>[https://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v511/n7507/full/nature13598.html Nature.com]</ref>

He was interested in [[tacit knowing]], a concept which [[Michael Polanyi]] and [[Shinichiro Kurimoto]] also developed.<ref>an essay titled 'SMALLTALK between [[AI]] and TK([[tacit knowing]])' from 'Contemporary Thought' (''[[Gendai Shisō]]'' 現代思想April 1987 published by Seidosha)</ref>

==Career==
Yamato was born at Tokyo in 1964.<ref name="dokidoki">[https://www.terumozaidan.or.jp/labo/interview/01/index.html　life science's DOKIDOKI laboratory]</ref> 
He graduated from [[Tokyo University]].<ref name="dokidoki" />

==Works==
